# Task 1: Data preparation and wrangling

### 1.1 Import the four CSV files

```{r t1q1}
emissionsRaw <- read_csv("data/Emissions.csv", trim_ws = TRUE)
renewablesRaw <- read_csv("data/Renewables.csv", trim_ws = TRUE)
consumptionRaw <- read_csv("data/Consumption.csv", trim_ws = TRUE)
countriesRaw <- read_csv("data/Countries.csv", trim_ws = TRUE)

glimpse(emissionsRaw)
glimpse(renewablesRaw)
glimpse(consumptionRaw)
glimpse(countriesRaw)

# summary(emissionsRaw)
# summary(renewablesRaw)
# summary(consumptionRaw)
# summary(countriesRaw)

# select(renewablesRaw, Country.Region)
```

### 1.2 Reshape `Renewables.csv` to one row per country per year

*Remember: this file contains rows that are not countries.*

```{r t1q2}
renewablesData <- renewablesRaw %>%
  filter(!Country.Region %in% c("World", "European Union (27)")) %>%
  rename(Country = Country.Region) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Country, 
               names_to = "Year", 
               values_to = "Renewables"
  )

head(renewablesData)
```

*What did you do with the non-country rows, and why?*

The 'World' and 'European Union (27)' totals overlap with the individual country observations. These aggregate rows were removed to prevent double counting and ensure the dataset only contains countries.

### 1.3 Rename the columns

```{r t1q3}
emissionsData <- emissionsRaw %>%
  rename(
    ISO = iso_code,
    Country = location,
    Region = region,
    Year = year,
    CO2 = annual_co2_mt,
    OilCO2 = annual_oil_co2_mt
  )

consumptionData <- consumptionRaw %>%
  rename(
    ISO = `Country Code`,
    ConsCO2 = `Consumption CO2`
  )

countriesData <- countriesRaw %>%
  rename(
    ISO = countryCode,
    Population = popData2022,
    GDPCapita = `GDP/capita`
  )
```

### 1.4 Make `Year` consistent across all data frames

```{r t1q4}
# Identifying incorrect years
consumptionData %>%
  # Detects all strings not containing exactly 4 digits
  filter(!str_detect(Year, "^\\d{4}$")) %>%
  select(ISO, Year) %>%
  head(10)

emissionsData <- emissionsData %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

renewablesData <- renewablesData %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

consumptionData <- consumptionData %>%
  mutate(
    # Capitalise all codes
    ISO = str_to_upper(ISO),
    # Extracts the dates from values containing additional characters
    Year = as.integer(str_extract(Year, "\\d{4}"))
  )
```
The consumption data frame is the only data frame containing inconsistent year values. 

### 1.5 Merge the five new variables into the master data frame

*Add `Renewables`, `ConsCO2`, `Population`, `GDP`, `GDPCapita`.*

```{r t1q5}
# Remove duplicate rows
emissionsData <- distinct(emissionsData)

# Fix differing country names in renewablesData
renewablesData <- renewablesData %>%
  mutate(
    Country = recode(
      Country,
      "Côte d'Ivoire" = "Cote d'Ivoire",
      "Congo, Dem. Rep." = "Democratic Republic of Congo",
      "Republic of Korea" = "South Korea",
      "United Republic of Tanzania" = "Tanzania"
    )
  )

# Correct Cameroons population scale
countriesData <- countriesData |>
  mutate(
    Population = if_else(ISO == "CMR",
      Population * 1000,
      Population
    )
  )

# Count how many emissions rows fail to match
unmatchedRenewables <- emissionsData %>%
  anti_join(
    renewablesData,
    by = c("Country", "Year")
  )

unmatchedConsumption <- emissionsData %>%
  anti_join(
    consumptionData,
    by = c("ISO", "Year")
  )

unmatchedCountries <- emissionsData %>%
  anti_join(
    countriesData,
    by = "ISO"
  )

# Return the count
joinAudit <- tibble(
  source = c("Renewables", "Consumption", "Countries"),
  unmatchedRows = c(
    nrow(unmatchedRenewables),
    nrow(unmatchedConsumption),
    nrow(unmatchedCountries)
  )
)

joinAudit
```

*How many rows failed to match on each join, and what did you do about them?*
